pectation that the instit gents, w ho found their attacks unavailing, would come to terms þÿ Further intelligence had been brought by native agents staling that another assault made on the British bad been likewise unsuccessful, and that although there had been fighting during the dav, the inhabitants of Cabul came eveiy night to sell flour and provisions to the troops in the cantonments. The war in China is of a different character ; and, as happened to Causer of old in his invasion of Gaul, our Commander in Chief upon tlie Chinese station may tiuly say, that he came, tie saw. and lie conquered : that the enemy always fly as he uppioaches, and that he iias only to take possession of tiie foils and cities which they abandon. In tiie attack upon Ningpo, appears it that after the citadel was carried by escalade, the garrison in the town refused to fight anv longer ; declining to obey their officers, and in a spirit of panic and fatalism, to which the Chinese are just as subject as ihe Mohammedans betook themselves to Might in a body. This principle, that of fatalism has been in all nations of the of the world the distinctive characteristic, of a barbnions people, arid whenever it begins to opeiule there is an effectual end ol all future resistance. It is the panic of a people and not of a mere army, and its effect is as

The Frigate with Lord Ashburton on board had not arrived; she left England Kith February- The Columbia steam packet at //alifax had 22 days passage, having met with damage in her machinery. The Mexicans who invaded Texas, had retreated, after taking San Antonio and carrying oti a good deal of plunder. President //ouston declared he would in retaliation, carry the war to the walls of Mexico. The Mexican force was much exaggerated.
